- When sentiment is low (≤0.5) or trending negative, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for 2–3 days.
- If 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend in history + low sentiment, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid mean reversion underestimation.
- Model consistently underestimates in early forecast horizon (days 1–5) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; apply +0.5–1.0% bias to first 5 days.
- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is rising, model often lags; forecast should be 1–2 days ahead of true trend; adjust by +0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
- If true outcome deviates >2% from 14-day moving average, model is misaligned; use 14-day MA as anchor for correction.
- For sentiment >0.7 and price >70, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3 days.
